verdict.strongest_covered_cluster: The failover and failback safety sequence is the strongest cluster: quorum/RPO-gated promotion, single writer lease, post-promotion routing, outbox resumption, checkout pause, safe retries, read-replica rejoin, validation, shadow traffic, and controlled writer return are all represented.
verdict.most_consequential_gap: Failure classification is only generic: the board does not enumerate the required instance, availability-zone, regional-service, database-write, and full-isolation categories.
verdict.coverage_summary: The board represents the three-region service topology and nearly all core failover, data, payment, recovery, and safety behavior. Eleven requirements are partial, chiefly because specific qualifiers or scopes are omitted: local catalog replicas during isolation, per-customer home-region selection, exactly two warm replicas, the five failure classes, automatic traffic removal, schema-specific quarantine, complete configuration provenance, complete audit-source coverage, and the two-surviving-region capacity boundary. Weighted coverage is 80 of 89, or 0.8989. No system-defining requirement is absent or contradicted, so no cap applies; under the threshold rubric this maps to 7.
